# ATST — ENS Social Media Account Attestation Format

> A signed claim that the owner of an ENS name also controls a particular
> social media account.

An attestation binds six data points: the user's wallet address, their ENS
name, the social media account identifier, the time of issuance, and the
attester's ENS name and wallet address. The envelope published on chain carries
only a version, a timestamp and a signature; every other field is reconstructed
by the verifier from ENS at verification time. Any change to the underlying
records after issuance breaks signature recovery, which is what makes the
attestation self-invalidating rather than merely stale.

## Specification

- [Full text](/llms-full.txt): The complete format, in plain text. Sections
  cover the claims, the DAG-CBOR payload, the CBOR envelope (tag 1635021684),
  issuance, the text record keys attestations[platform][attester] and
  uid[platform][attester], verification, failure modes, and the handle
  persistence variant.
- [Rendered spec](/): The same document as a web page.

## Related

- ATST Playground: Verify an attestation step by step, take an envelope apart,
  or sign one with a throwaway key. Exposes a machine-callable verification
  endpoint described by its own /.well-known/agent-card.json.
- [Text Record Attestations](https://github.com/ensdomains/ensips/pull/85): This
  format as a pending ENSIP, open for review at the time of writing.
- [ENSIP-27](https://docs.ens.domains/ensip/27): The related ENS improvement
  proposal.
- [Lighthouse](https://lighthouse.cx/): Runs this attestation service. The
  attester's ENS name is atst.lighthousegov.eth.

## Notes

This host serves the specification only. It has no API.
